 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Terry McLaurin will miss his third straight game when the Washington Commanders face the New York Giants on "Thursday Night Football." McLaurin suffered a torn patellar tendon in his left knee during Washington's Oct. 19 game against the San Francisco 49ers.
 The injury occurred in the first quarter of the Commanders' 23-17 loss. McLaurin went down while running a route, and medical staff eventually carted him off the field with his left leg in an air cast.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed the following day that an MRI revealed the torn patellar tendon and that McLaurin would miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season. He required surgery to repair the injury, which was performed on Oct. 30. 
 Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin (17)Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images
 The Commanders subsequently placed McLaurin on injured reserve on Oct. 28, officially removing him from their active roster. 
 McLaurin's latest injury occurred just two weeks after he returned from a hamstring issue that forced him to miss Washington's Week 4 game against the Indianapolis Colts. He returned in Week 5 against the Giants before suffering the knee injury the following week.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement McLaurin has appeared in five games this season, recording 15 receptions for 230 yards and one touchdown. The 31-year-old also missed seven games because of multiple injuries last season. 
 As a result, Washington will have to finish the season without one of its leading offensive weapons. Stefon Diggs and Treylon Burks will be expected to shoulder more responsibility while McLaurin works toward his recovery.
 The Commanders are 2-5-1 entering Thursday's game, and will need to start stacking up wins to stay alive in the NFC East.
